loop.top3_series_pattern: strong long‑run trend + strong seasonality, moderate predictability, unstable model ranking across windows
loop.top3_why: The mean of the full pool is a simple, robust combination that performs consistently across the three validation windows (per_window values are all close to each other). Given the unstable ranking and high correlation among many models, a deterministic baseline such as the mean is less likely to overfit to noise in the validation windows than a weighted scheme that relies on noisy error estimates. The weighted inverse‑error strategy (A) shows a slightly higher per‑window variance and depends on unstable weight estimates, while the DBA (B) has a very high per‑window error in the first window, indicating sensitivity to the particular validation split. Therefore the plain mean (C) is expected to generalize best to the blind test window.
loop.top3_why_not: A may overfit to the validation windows because the weights are derived from noisy error estimates and the ranking is unstable. B, though deterministic, shows a large error in the first window and relies on DTW alignment that can be sensitive to the specific sample; its overall performance is not consistently better than the mean. Hence C is preferred.
